note: Listening links open a named model in the companion explorer. A matching mathematical model is not proof of a person’s exclusive preference, every performance, or regional prevalence. The linked explorer starts silently and requires Enable sound.

statusDescriptions.source-model: Corresponds to a mathematical method or ideal explicitly discussed in the supplied source; does not certify an instrument’s actual tuning.
statusDescriptions.representative: A modern listening reconstruction of a reported or inferred family; the exact numerical recipe is not established.
statusDescriptions.comparison: A deliberately labelled comparison, not an attribution to the historical person or work.

tunings.label: Quarter-comma meantone
tunings.description: Narrow fifths and pure major thirds in a twelve-note keyboard model.
tunings.caveat: A specific ideal keyboard layout. Association with a person may be a modern listening reconstruction, rather than an exact documented recipe.

tunings.label: Two-sevenths-comma meantone
tunings.description: The generating fifth is narrowed by 2/7 of the syntonic comma; the C–E third is about 383.24 cents.
tunings.caveat: Uses the exact ideal C-based layout supplied with the Preferences research, rounded to twelve decimal places. The dated theoretical prescription does not establish every performance of Zarlino’s music.

tunings.label: Third-comma meantone
tunings.description: A meantone model with pure minor thirds; one of the alternatives discussed by Salinas.
tunings.caveat: The label “Salinas temperament” should not hide his discussion of several usable meantone variants.

tunings.label: Werckmeister III
tunings.description: A circulating unequal temperament with several sizes of major third.
tunings.caveat: A defined modern standard reconstruction. It is neither a unique Bach tuning nor evidence for the former, retracted attribution to Buxtehude’s Lübeck organ.

tunings.label: Kirnberger III
tunings.description: A circulating unequal temperament retaining a pure C–E third.
tunings.caveat: A named comparison model. The examined Türk table of contents mentions Kirnberger’s method without establishing that this exact variant was intended.

tunings.label: Vallotti
tunings.description: A mild circulating unequal model with contrasting key colours.
tunings.caveat: Used here as a listening comparison where the research recommends mild circulating tunings; this does not attribute Vallotti’s recipe to Bach or C. P. E. Bach.

tunings.label: 12 equal divisions
tunings.description: Twelve equal 100-cent steps per octave; major thirds are 400 cents.
tunings.caveat: An ideal mathematical model. A theoretical recommendation or historical report does not establish exact acoustic realization or general regional adoption.

tunings.label: 31 equal divisions
tunings.description: Thirty-one equal steps per octave, approximately 38.71 cents each.
tunings.caveat: A modern comparison for Vicentino’s extended pitch resources, not an exact reconstruction of the Archicembalo or a claim that 36 physical keys equal 31 pitches.

mappingNotes.schlick1511: The research verified bibliographic details, not a numerical recipe; no tuning is assigned.
mappingNotes.louis_couperin_repertoire: The research recommends a documented French unequal reconstruction. No such exact recipe is supplied in the audited explorer presets, so no substitute is assigned.
mappingNotes.buxtehude_luebeck: The former Werckmeister III attribution was retracted. This atlas assigns no precise tuning to Buxtehude’s organ.
mappingNotes.leopold_mozart_1756: Adjustable violin and ensemble intonation does not specify one fixed keyboard temperament.
mappingNotes.wa_mozart_forschungsfrage: The supplied research leaves Mozart’s personal numerical tuning open; no preset is assigned from bibliographic metadata or location.
mappingNotes.beethoven_offener_befund: The supplied source selection establishes no personal tuning instruction; no preference is inferred from Vienna or a general teaching source.
